q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
report:
Yes on the raw numbers: comparing games on the same network, smaller crowds went with smaller national TV audiences (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62). Mostly no after comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, so popular teams do not drive the result: the correlation falls to 0.16 in 2025 (range -0.05 to 0.37) and 0.14 in 2026 (range -0.08 to 0.34), and both ranges include zero (table: crowd_tv_headline).

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like. These are associations, not cause and effect.*

q: Why did the Mets over-perform on attendance in 2025?
report:
The New York Mets' home attendance surged in 2025, with actual average attendance growing by 35.9% from the season before to reach 39,776 fans per game (table: team_season_model). This turnout was 23.6% higher than what the prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market size would predict (table: team_season_model). Part of this may be a rebound: the team was 18.8% below its prediction the season before (table: team_season_model). In comparison, the 2025 actual average of 39,776 fans per game was higher than the 2024 average of 29,268 fans per game by 10,508 fans per game (table: team_season_model). These strong crowds coincided with the franchise signing outfielder Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million contract in December 2024 ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)). The team also added starting pitchers Frankie Montas and Griffin Canning during the offseason ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)), and opened the season with a stellar 45–24 record through June 12 ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)).

q: What drives MLB attendance?
report:
MLB attendance closely coincides with game-level factors like home openers, specific opponents, and the day of the week, as well as team-level factors like recent winning records and past crowds. At the team level, a season win rate .100 higher coincides with an 8.6% increase in attendance, while a 10% higher crowd over the prior two years goes with an 8.2% increase (table: model_coefficients). A metro population 10% larger has a 0.2% association, though this does not show a clear effect (table: model_coefficients). A team's overall season attendance is highly predictable, with a model capturing 90.2% of the differences between teams, while game-by-game attendance is also highly predictable, with a model capturing 82.6% of the variation overall, 43.2% of the variation within the same stadium, and a prediction error of 0.193 (table: model_fit). At the game level, home openers coincide with a 69.1% jump in attendance (table: model_coefficients). Games against the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees go with increases of 25.0% and 15.7% respectively, while a .100 higher home win rate is associated with a 4.7% increase (table: model_coefficients). Conversely, Monday games coincide with a 21.8% drop compared to Fridays, Wednesday games with a 20.6% drop, Tuesday games with an 18.9% drop, and March and April games with a 10.9% drop compared to August (table: model_coefficients).

*These are associations, not cause and effect.*

q: How did the Cubs do on attendance and viewership last year?
report:
During the 2025 season, the Chicago Cubs drew strong crowds with an average fill rate of 89.9% at the ballpark (table: games_clean) and averaged 1,030,818 viewers for their single-game national television appearances (table: team_tv_summary). On television, the Cubs made 17 total national appearances, including 12 single-game broadcasts, 5 Fox window appearances, and 2 special event games (table: team_tv_summary). q: How did Cubs day games compare with night games on attendance in 2025?
report: Chicago Cubs home day games in 2025 had higher average attendance than night games by 1,714 (37,780 compared to 36,067), with fill rates of 91.5% and 87.3% respectively (table: games_clean). This difference in attendance is linked to the weekday schedule composition, as weekends consist overwhelmingly of day games (39 day versus 3 night games) while weekdays feature most of the night games (27 night versus 10 day games) (table: games_clean). When comparing day versus night games directly on individual weekdays, attendance levels are comparable, indicating the difference is a byproduct of scheduling rather than a general preference for day games (table: games_clean). Additionally, day games consistently outdraw or closely match night games within individual months from April through September (table: games_clean).
